barriers.reason: The patient works 7:00 AM–3:30 PM at a warehouse and drives for Uber until 10 PM, so a Wednesday 1:00 PM educator visit would cost half a shift and a write-up; the patient can only come after 4 PM or Saturday morning.

alternatives.text: Ask the diabetes educator for an after-4 PM weekday slot or a Saturday morning visit so the patient does not miss work.
Schedule the insulin-teaching visit on the same day/campus as another visit the patient already attends, or use telehealth if a hands-on exam is not needed.

barriers.reason: On work days the patient eats coffee and gas-station food between jobs, with reliable meals only on weekends, so a carb-consistent packed lunch is hard to obtain.

alternatives.text: Have the dialysis/renal dietitian redesign the diet around foods the patient can actually get on work days, including renal-friendly gas-station and convenience options.
Screen for SNAP through Illinois ABE to improve the food budget for work-day meals.
Use a food pantry on the patient's non-treatment days, but pair it with the renal dietitian since pantry food is often not renal-friendly.
